What is StudyFetch?

Student study platform that turns uploaded course materials - lecture slides, PDFs, notes, recorded lectures - into flashcards, practice tests, summaries and an AI tutor called Spark.E that answers questions from those materials.

Best for

Converting course materials into active-recall study assets.

Main features

  • Upload lectures/PDFs/slides and auto-generate flashcards, quizzes and notes
  • Spark.E AI tutor grounded in your materials
  • lecture recording and transcription
  • spaced-repetition flashcards
  • practice tests with explanations
  • study-time analytics
  • Classroom mode for instructors.

Practical use cases

  • Turning a semester of lecture slides into a flashcard deck
  • generating a practice exam before finals
  • transcribing and summarising a recorded lecture
  • asking questions about course content at 2am.

Who is it for?

  • University and secondary students, tutoring centres, some instructors.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium subscription with student discounts

Plans described in the source

Free tier with limited uploads and generations. Premium around $4.99-9.99/mo billed annually (higher monthly). Annual plans commonly around $50-100/yr. Educator/classroom plans quoted separately. Verify - StudyFetch runs frequent promotions and prices vary.

Free plan

Yes - limited free tier.

Free trial

Trials and heavy student discounts offered regularly.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier caps uploads, flashcard sets, tutor messages and recording minutes per month.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Very cheap for students
  • the materials-grounded tutor avoids the generic-answer problem
  • flashcard and practice-test generation from real course content is a genuine time saver
  • spaced repetition is built in.

Limitations to consider

  • Generated questions can be shallow or miss the point of the material
  • transcription accuracy varies with audio quality and accent
  • limited depth for technical or mathematical content
  • less institutional credibility than Khan Academy
  • data-handling disclosures are thinner than enterprise tools.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension

Languages

  • Multiple languages supported; strongest in English

API access

No public API

Integrations and exports

  • Canvas, Google Drive, PDF/PPT/DOCX upload, lecture recording

Evaluation notes

Generated practice questions should be checked against the actual assessment style of the course - they tend toward recall rather than application. Best used alongside, not instead of, reading the source material.
